description:

Superhuman Docs https://superhuman.com/docs is where teams and AI get their best work done together. It brings documents, data, workflows, project management, and knowledge into one flexible collaborative surface.

One team is building new product experiences within Docs, taking ideas from early exploration through launch and iteration. The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination.

n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.



Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:



 - Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

 - Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

 - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register.



We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.


STAFF PLATFORM ENGINEER, AGENTIC ENGINEERING

Developer Productivity · AI Coding Agents · Developer Platform

Our ambition: an engineering organisation where humans and agents work as one continuously learning system, turning frontier AI capabilities and real-world feedback into more ambitious product development. We want n8n to be the reference for how this is done, without compromising quality, resilience or trust. Your main goal is to make that real.



This is a Staff individual contributor role in Developer Platform and the technical driving force behind ACDC (Agent-centric Development Cycle), our engineering-wide initiative for agentic development. Nobody has a playbook for this yet. You'll write ours.



You won't start from zero. Agents wired into Linear already automate around 80% of the development cycle on one of our developer platform projects, alongside pilots for insight, feature-flag and PR-review agents and a shared agent harness. Your job is to take this from promising experiments to the way n8n builds software.



This role is for someone who thinks about this problem constantly. You run agents all day, rebuild your own workflow every time the frontier moves, and have more ideas than time. 



You'll stay hands-on, building the first versions yourself, and shape how the work grows beyond one person.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


SET DIRECTION AND OWN THE OUTCOME

 - Identify where agentic development can make the greatest difference, using developer feedback, existing experiments and engineering performance data.

 - Set the strategy and priorities across agent execution, repository readiness, CI, security and developer workflows.

 - Make build, buy or pass decisions on tools and vendors, and own the cost and value trade-offs, including AI spend.

 - Make decisions where requirements are incomplete and the trade-offs between autonomy, reliability, security and review effort are still emerging.

 - Build alignment through technical proposals, clear decisions and working software, and report progress and impact to engineering leadership.


BUILD THE FOUNDATIONS

 - Design and build isolated execution environments where agents can work with the right access to code, tools and context, without exposing secrets or sensitive systems.

 - Own the safety model: which task categories agents may attempt, what they must never touch, and where human review is required, partnering with Security on sensitive areas like auth, billing, permissions and data handling.

 - Make n8n's monorepo agent-ready, working with Architecture and senior engineers on repo structure, testability, boundaries and the context agents need.


INTEGRATE AGENTS INTO HOW WE WORK

 - Build repeatable workflows that take Linear issues through agent execution, self-verification and review to merged PRs, across a growing range of task types.

 - Integrate agentic workflows with GitHub, CI, test infrastructure and code review, so the agentic path becomes the easiest path for engineers.

 - Extend the loop beyond coding: connect earlier signals like product research and customer requests, and later ones like production metrics, so agents contribute across the whole cycle.

 - Open it up beyond engineering, so PMs, designers and others can turn a well-defined issue into a reviewed, mergeable change.

 - Shape review practices, such as PR evidence that shows what changed, what ran, what risks remain and where human judgment is needed.


MEASURE WHAT WORKS

 - Build benchmarks from real historical engineering tasks to evaluate output quality, failure modes, review burden and production risk.

 - Define and track quality and adoption signals, such as reviewer acceptance rate, CI pass rate, rework rate and developer satisfaction.

 - Use data and feedback to change course, retire what doesn't work, and build trust across engineering.


REQUIREMENTS


MUST-HAVES

 - 🔥 Frontier obsession: You live at the frontier. You try new models and tools as they land, and you have strong, evidence-backed opinions on what's real and what's hype.

title: Senior Data Integration Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join a small engineering team at a growth-stage logistics software company focused on shipment visibility and risk management for temperature-sensitive goods. You will own the integrations that turn data from devices, carriers, and customer systems into reliable information teams can act on.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and operate ingestion pipelines for device telemetry, carrier milestones, and customer order data using APIs, webhooks, polling, files, and queues.

 - Map and normalize source data into shared shipment and telemetry models, with validation and quality checks throughout the pipeline.

 - Monitor pipeline health, build alerts and dashboards, and handle replays or backfills when data is late or incorrect.

 - Use partner API specifications and sample data to deliver new integrations.

 - Turn one-off integrations into reusable, configuration-driven pipelines.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - At least 5 years of experience building production data pipelines or backend data systems, with ownership of external integrations from ingestion through monitoring and support.

 - Strong Python skills and familiarity with TypeScript or Node.js, or the ability to ramp up quickly.

 - Proficiency with SQL, data modeling, batch and incremental ETL/ELT, schema mapping, and data quality practices.

 - Experience integrating external APIs, including rate limits, retries, and pagination, as well as operating cloud services on Azure or AWS.

 - Hands-on experience with testing, CI/CD, monitoring, and observability for production systems.

 - Experience with IoT, telemetry, logistics, regulated data, event-driven systems, or data processing tools such as Spark is a plus.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary is $140,000 to $180,000 annually, with equity and a cash bonus. Visa sponsorship is available.


LOCATION

Remote within the United States.

An overview of this role
We are looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Change Record team within GitLab’s Source Code stage . As AI agents increasingly write code alongside people, every change needs a clear, trustworthy record of what changed, why, and who or what made it. You’ll build that record into GitLab’s source code experience, for humans and agents alike. This is a backend-focused role for an engineer with full-stack experience who enjoys balancing work on existing systems with new product development.
That work happens in one of GitLab’s oldest and most complex product areas, where you’ll use Ruby on Rails to improve a critical system serving GitLab.com, self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated. Source Code provides the interface layer, through Gitaly, to the Git repositories behind a large share of GitLab traffic, so you’ll help keep it reliable through performance tuning, caching, rate limiting, observability, and resiliency, collaborating with product, design, security, Gitaly, Code Review, and Source Code Experience teams. Supporting production systems and improving established experiences are central to the role, especially while you’re onboarding, and over time you’ll also help build experiences for developers working with agents.
You'll work remotely from the United Kingdom or Poland.
What you’ll do
• Develop secure, well-tested, performant features and improvements using Ruby on Rails and GraphQL, among other technologies.
• Work through complex requirements and legacy constraints to deliver clear solutions while protecting the reliability of this critical system.
• Design and maintain backend services, APIs, data models, and business logic that support intuitive source code workflows.
• Collaborate across functions and teams, both asynchronously and synchronously, and involve domain experts when their input will improve the outcome.
• Use AI agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output.
• Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and contribute to constructive code reviews.
• Help strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, contributing to root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency.
• Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others.
• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you’ll bring
• Professional experience building backend web applications, services, or application programming interfaces, with experience using Ruby and GraphQL.
• An understanding of relational databases, structured query language, data modeling, caching, background processing, and backend performance practices.
• Experience with full-stack development to build and maintain user-facing workflows and their underlying systems.
• Experience writing backend unit and integration tests, with familiarity with the testing pyramid, Git, and collaborative code review processes.
• Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including sharing useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment.
• The ability to manage assigned priorities, work through ambiguity, take ownership of your work, and seek guidance when needed.
• Experience using AI coding agents to speed up software development while critically reviewing their output.
• Bonus: you’ve built agents or agent-based workflows that run in production, not just prototypes.
About the team
The functional team works across Europe and North America, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration. It includes four engineers, comprising both backend and frontend engineers. We work closely with other Source Code teams, Agentic Preview, Repository Services, and Hardening, as well as other teams in the company such as the Gitaly team, and the AI Governance team.

description:

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. GitLab engineers increasingly build software with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but they can also produce passing test suites for software that doesn't work as intended. As a Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, you'll own the technical thesis for closing that validation gap and build the early proof yourself. You'll rethink what validation means when the author is an agent and make the feedback loop fast, automatic, and trustworthy enough that teams choose to adopt it.
• Validation that confirms agent-generated code does what was intended, so a passing suite means a working feature and not just a satisfied proxy.
• Mid-loop feedback that helps an agent self-correct toward working software instead of green assertions.
• Language-aware approaches under one shared model of what "trusted" means, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, while allowing the right technique to differ by language.
• Real measurement of whether engineers trust and adopt the path, fed straight back into the platform.
What you’ll do
• Own the technical thesis for how GitLab validates software when an agent is the author, and turn it into an architecture the team can build against.
• Prototype the hard parts by building early versions of feedback mechanisms that catch the gap between passing tests and working software, proving what works before the team scales it.
• Develop approaches for GitLab's primary stacks, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, under one shared definition of "trusted," while allowing the right technique to differ by language.
• Design the mid-loop feedback an agent needs to self-correct toward working software rather than green assertions, and build the systems that deliver it.
• Collaborate with engineering teams to adopt these approaches, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those findings to improve the platform.
• Set technical direction the team can build on, review designs, and help teammates grow their technical judgment.
• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you’ll bring
• Deep, current, hands-on experience building real software with artificial intelligence agents, ideally across more than one language, and a clear understanding of why agent output can pass tests yet fail in production.
• A strong point of view on the validation gap and concrete ideas for closing it, backed by approaches you've built or tried.
• Experience designing distributed systems designed to run on Kubernetes first.
• The technical range to design systems rather than tune a single framework, and the judgment to know when a solution should be general or language-specific.
• You prototype to learn, and you ship.
• The ability to influence engineers across an organization without formal authority through working code and sound reasoning.
• Strong written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.
• Alignment with GitLab's values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.
This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We aren't looking for depth in a particular testing framework. We're looking for someone who has built with agents, experienced the validation gap firsthand, and wants to solve it.
About the team
The Trusted Agentic Development team is part of GitLab's Developer Experience group. We build platforms and practices that help GitLab engineers validate agent-generated software with confidence. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.
